payload.title: The council asked residents what they thought of its 2026/27 budget
payload.summary: For five weeks from 4 December 2025 the council ran a survey on its Get Talking Norwich site, promoted by text alert to 120,000 residents. It asked about a 2.99% council tax rise, a new "live budget" reviewed during the year, and a ring-fenced Readiness Fund for the costs of local government reorganisation. 899 people answered, well down on the post-2019 average of 1,361.
detail: For the first time in seven years, more respondents opposed the council tax rise than supported it: 430 of 899 opposed or strongly opposed it and 248 supported it, with 221 neutral.
The council states plainly that "no specific factors have been identified to explain the variation in response rate".
Consulting business ratepayers is a legal duty. Consulting residents is the council's own choice.
